issue.description:
Owns the doctor surface of the Phase 7 host-local upstream contract (auto-split of twill-ab007a11; depends on twill-c4e00404 so window and coverage-gap semantics it reports on are settled first). Target file: docs/notes/host-report-contract.md, section "Doctor per-host coverage". Much of this surface is already on main (commits 5641877, efed009) - verify each criterion against committed state and complete any gap; do not rewrite wholesale. This is the contract side only: twill-5c404a45 owns the doctor implementation.

Acceptance criteria, all verifiable in the committed docs:
- Roster evaluation: doctor evaluates the configured host roster including hosts that have never produced a record; for each host it reports host_id, state, last accepted generated_at, last reported ingest success, most recent covered UTC date, retained coverage gaps, and a reason; timestamps come from the accepted report, never from git commit time, file mtime, or the most recent event timestamp; a host with zero observations can be healthy.
- State table: current = valid report at most 72 hours old AND reported ingest success at most 72 hours old AND no known coverage gap in the last 30 dates, reported healthy for that host; stale_host = expected host never reported, either timestamp older than 72 hours, or current-window coverage missing, reported degraded with the specific missing or stale signal.
- Invalid candidate: adds a candidate_error diagnostic and degrades the check without replacing the last accepted report or resetting that report age; the host state still reflects the last accepted report.
- Aggregate semantics: the host-coverage check is degraded (doctor exit 1) if any expected host is stale or has an invalid candidate; an absent or silent remote host MUST NOT turn the local ingest or detector run into a failed run or a broken (exit 2) doctor verdict; local corruption and local timer failures keep their existing health semantics.
- Cross-host finding attribution: a finding may say a signature occurred on two hosts only when two accepted reports contain positive evidence in the detector window, even if one host has since gone stale; it MUST show contributing host ids, evidence dates, and freshness states, and MUST NOT claim a stale or missing host had zero occurrences or that fleet coverage is complete; recovery is a validated fresh report with contiguous current coverage, never an inference from silence.

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md section 9, Phase 9B; sections 7.1.1 and 10.2.

Outcome: derive source-linked execution episodes that distinguish an active authorized outcome from a new request, settled decisions, legitimate waits and unknown context.

Acceptance:
1. Build the versioned episode/assertion projection from the interaction contract, storing objective, pending actions, scope/resource constraints, explicit approval and revocation, questions, external waits and observed completion with references and known/inferred/unknown evidence strength.
2. Status questions preserve the active objective; explicit replacement/cancellation/material scope changes split it. Match actual interactive answers to their question identity. Conservative action/resource equivalence and explicit same-outcome resumption are required. Assistant promises, generic continue, silence, current rules and reversibility cannot establish historical authority.
3. Captured historical instructions or effective-time instruction records are distinct from today's coverage corpus. Missing policy/terminality, omitted material context or uncertain scope remains unknown. Preserve proposal/permission holds and advice-only request classification.
4. Raw-shaped CLI fixtures cover the same action with prior approval, withheld approval, changed scope, cancellation, question answers, stale rules, independent tasks, worker boilerplate and sidechain handoffs; output is deterministic and invalidated/rederived when evidence/version changes. Include schema/cursor/rebuild/retention tests and public contract docs.

Authority and boundaries: explicitly requested Phase 9 implementation; see docs/plan/plan.md, 2026-10-23 admission. Public engine and newly authored synthetic fixtures only. Source evidence, real labels, generated lessons/guards and evaluation reports remain private. Preserve existing proposal holds, the no-auto-apply rule, archive independence, stdlib-only core and the existing Explain call/byte budgets. No supervisor, session resumption, new model backend or deployment change. Scope-expansion discoveries stay proposals.

Delivery: own implementation, necessary tests, contract/docs updates, verification and delivery on this bead. Run scripts/definition-of-done.sh from /home/coding/TWILL; record actual outcomes and incomplete checks in notes. Use raw-shaped synthetic sources through the real CLI, not manually seeded observations to claim ingestion coverage. Work on main, preserve unrelated edits, stage precise paths, push only origin, and close with a reason after verified delivery.

issue.description:
Plan: docs/plan/plan.md section 9, Phase 9E; sections 7.1.1 and 10.2.

Outcome: evaluate detector quality and observed autonomy improvement through the existing private measure/trend/digest pipeline with explicit opportunity denominators and missingness.

Acceptance:
1. Report eligible execution-turn opportunities, terminal-state coverage, candidates by disposition, supported findings, explicit human restart/approval exchanges and unknown/unassessed counts by source, detector/analyzer version and window. Deduplicate one intervention detected by several families. Rates require comparable nonzero known denominators; missing or unreviewed data is not zero or a negative example.
2. Private adjudicated labels support precision/abstention evaluation. Record intervention dates and comparable before/after windows in the existing private measurement stream. Elapsed intervals are observational; token/cost values require matching telemetry, are null when missing and never attribute whole-session cost to one exchange. Do not claim causality or completed outcomes without evidence.
3. Cluster/session/week/weekly/backtest measurement replays the same supported/version-matching membership; changed rubric/parser bumps analyzer and affected detector versions. Preserve historical evidence and intervention attribution across rebuild without modifying accepted lesson content.
4. Public synthetic golden/scenario fixtures exercise all five positives, mandatory negatives, sparse labels, changed source coverage, missing telemetry, version drift, overlapping families, empty windows and replay idempotence. Run final CLI pipeline Scenarios 5-7 and all existing required gates. Real evaluation labels, incident reports and measurements stay private; do not commit copied/anonymized real cases.

Authority and boundaries: explicitly requested Phase 9 implementation; see docs/plan/plan.md, 2026-10-23 admission. Public engine and newly authored synthetic fixtures only. Source evidence, real labels, generated lessons/guards and evaluation reports remain private. Preserve existing proposal holds, the no-auto-apply rule, archive independence, stdlib-only core and the existing Explain call/byte budgets. No supervisor, session resumption, new model backend or deployment change. Scope-expansion discoveries stay proposals.

Delivery: own implementation, necessary tests, contract/docs updates, verification and delivery on this bead. Run scripts/definition-of-done.sh from /home/coding/TWILL; record actual outcomes and incomplete checks in notes. Use raw-shaped synthetic sources through the real CLI, not manually seeded observations to claim ingestion coverage. Work on main, preserve unrelated edits, stage precise paths, push only origin, and close with a reason after verified delivery.

Locked compatibility/coverage: retain existing twill-measurement/v1 rows unchanged. Use section 7.1.1 private autonomy/impact/YYYY-MM-DD.json and autonomy/interventions.jsonl via the additive extension. Each historical replay reports assessed/eligible coverage; unassessed/invalidated candidate windows are unknown, cannot become verified-zero points or automatically resolve a lesson. Test reversal plus rebuild against an already accepted lesson without editing its immutable content.
issue.notes: Authorized by the operator request to update the plan and create implementable worker beads. Scope and acceptance are fixed in the description and admitted Phase 9. Waiting for the upstream planning/implementation dependency; do not bypass it or modify existing holds. Start by reading the plan, applicable AGENTS.md, predecessor evidence and current worktree. Keep progress, actual verification, delivery references and next action here.

Acceptance criteria, all verifiable in the committed docs:
- Exactly one current snapshot per host; a valid v1 report has exactly these top-level fields with UTC RFC 3339 Z timestamps: schema, host_id, generated_at, last_ingest_success_at, window_start, window_end, signature_scheme, records; unknown top-level fields are rejected.
- Record schema exact: each record has exactly day (UTC YYYY-MM-DD), kind (one of run_failed, tool_error, tool_rejected, hook_denial), signature_sha256 (64 lowercase hex), sessions, events, first_seen, last_seen; counts are positive integers; first_seen/last_seen within day and ordered; at most one record per (day, kind, signature_sha256), sorted by that tuple.
- Aggregate semantics pinned: sessions counts distinct local sessions in the bucket, events counts capped local observations; a session spanning two dates contributes once per date, so summing daily sessions is not a distinct-session count for a window; the cross-host detector counts distinct hosts with evidence, not a sum of session counts.
- Hash-only identity: exporter selects post-redaction local observations with a nonempty normalized signature and one of the four kinds; it stores the full SHA-256 of the normalized signature; the local 12-character sig_hash prefix MUST NOT be used as cross-host identity; signature_scheme is twill-normalized-signature-sha256/v1 and changes when redaction/normalization/hashing changes grouping, which also forces a new host-report major version; consumers never merge across schemes; no record contains the normalized signature itself; the namespace stays private (never the public repo, never the Phase 8 recall index).
- Privacy enumeration: v1 permits no free-form text in records - no transcript line, command, excerpt, normalized signature, program name, tool output, repository or filesystem path, rule text, session id, cursor, usage row, or model prompt; unknown record fields rejected; strings validated for format and length before publication.
- Bounds: at most 16 MiB UTF-8 and 50,000 records; exceeding either fails that publication loudly - never truncate, sample, or publish a partial snapshot that looks complete.
- Freshness sanity: last_ingest_success_at not later than generated_at; generated_at no more than five minutes ahead of the consumer clock; a report older than the last accepted one for the host is rejected; an equal timestamp is an idempotent retry only with identical bytes.
- A valid empty-report example (empty records array, advancing generated_at and last_ingest_success_at) is present and itself satisfies the field rules.

issue.description:
Split child of twill-03739b8a; depends on twill-6e777a09.

codex_reader.py only parses whole files — it has no offset handling at all. Plan section 6.2 step 4 requires the reader to seek to the cursor's last_offset and parse complete lines only, so the hourly ingest does not reparse a rollout from byte 0. Add an incremental API to codex_reader.py (e.g. parse_rollout(path, last_offset=0) -> ParseResult carrying bytes_consumed / next_offset) that: seeks to last_offset; discards a trailing partial line; feeds only complete lines to the line parser; keeps the pending-call state machine and token-usage snapshot conversion correct across the resume boundary. Semantics must match the appended-between-runs codex fixture: parsing base then append from the recorded offset yields the same event stream as parsing the whole file.

Scope boundary: do NOT touch cursor storage, identity hashing, or reparse-triggering — that is twill-9d2c452f. This bead owns the parser side only.

Acceptance criteria:
1. New tests prove base-then-append resume equals the whole-file event stream on the codex fixtures, including a truncated trailing line at the resume point.

issue.description: Plan section 8.4. Additive-only migrations with a downgrade that keeps unknown columns, so a rolled-back release still reads a newer DB. Consumers are later-phase schema additions, not the v1 tables.
issue.notes:
Implemented in twill_schema.py, commit fc5bf03.

Design (plan §8.4):
- Migration dataclass + MIGRATIONS registry; ships EMPTY — the v1 tables are the baseline (V1_SCHEMA + inline _apply_additive_columns), not migration consumers; later-phase schema additions append Migration entries.
- Additive-only enforced mechanically at import (_validated/_validate_statement): whitelist of 'CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS' (table/index/unique index/virtual table/view) and 'ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN', one statement per entry (no embedded semicolons — this excludes triggers by design), contiguous versions from BASELINE_VERSION=1, unique names. A DROP/rename/CREATE-without-IF-NOT-EXISTS fails the process at startup, not half-applied on a database.
- run_migrations: unstamped databases stamp baseline 1; pending migrations apply inside one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction whose commit records meta.schema_version — a failed statement rolls the whole run back (stamp and DDL together). ALTER entries route through the same add-if-missing check as baseline convergence, so re-runs are no-ops.
- Downgrade tolerance: a database stamped above this release's newest migration opens untouched — no statement runs, stamp never lowered, unknown columns/tables kept; the older writer can still insert via named columns. _verify_observation_shape relaxed from exact equality to prefix match so a rolled-back release READS a newer DB that appended observation columns (exact-match would have refused it — that was the one place an older release could not read a newer DB). Pre-v1 Phase 0 shape still rejected with the rebuild hint.

Tests (tests/test_schema.py, +7): baseline stamping + shipped-registry-empty pin; apply-in-order + stamp + idempotent reopen; whole-run rollback on a failed migration; rolled-back-release-reads-newer-DB (writer + read-only + named-column insert); read-only open never stamps; validator rejects non-additive statements and non-contiguous/duplicate/empty names. test_meta_enforces_key_value_state_contract reseeded — the runner now owns the schema_version row. Makefile gains a 'make test' target (unittest discover).
